profile.name: Siva Bhargav Korrapati
profile.tagline: I build backend systems and study what makes AI systems reliable in production.
profile.specialization: Backend Architecture · RAG & LLM Integration · Cloud Infrastructure
profile.bio: Software Engineer with 4+ years building scalable backend systems across banking, fintech, and healthcare, specializing in Python, FastAPI, and event-driven distributed architectures. I bring applied AI experience through RAG and LLM-powered workflows in production healthcare systems, plus graduate research into LLM reliability, prompting, retrieval, and lightweight model adaptation. I care about building production-grade systems that hold up — backend engineering paired with AI that actually works.

experience.summary: Building the backend for financial workflows: transaction processing, loan servicing, and account data at scale.
highlights: Architected 12+ backend microservices in FastAPI and PostgreSQL, using query optimization and async request processing to improve API performance across financial workflows.
Designed secure, reusable REST APIs for high-volume transaction processing with validation, retry mechanisms, and centralized error handling.
Orchestrated event-driven integrations using message queues to synchronize loan servicing and payment workflows, cutting processing delays during peak periods.
Implemented Redis caching for frequently accessed account data, reducing database load and improving dashboard responsiveness.
Automated CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Actions and Docker, cutting deployment time from 40 minutes to under 12.

experience.summary: Built the backend for WeKare360, orchestrating AI transcription, summarization, and consultation workflows for healthcare.
highlights: Engineered backend services in Node.js and Express.js to orchestrate AI-powered transcription, summarization, and consultation workflows.
Integrated AI summarization pipelines with MongoDB-backed storage, designing flexible schemas for structured and unstructured consultation data.
Designed REST and GraphQL APIs enabling semantic retrieval over consultation transcripts and AI-generated summaries.
Built workflows converting AI-extracted action items into reminders and scheduling events.
Developed permission-based APIs for sharing consultation recordings between patients and care teams, enforcing application-level access controls.

experience.summary: Researched LLM reliability, retrieval-augmented generation, and lightweight model adaptation, translating findings into practical trade-off guidance.
highlights: Investigated reliability challenges across proprietary and open-weight LLMs through zero-shot, few-shot, and instruction-based prompting experiments, identifying prompt sensitivity and unsupported responses.
Extended the research into Retrieval-Augmented Generation, building a document chunking, embedding, and vector-based semantic retrieval pipeline to ground LLM responses in external source material.
Explored lightweight adaptation approaches using LoRA, QLoRA, and PEFT, and studied RLHF/DPO to determine when model adaptation was preferable to prompting or retrieval.
Built Python-based evaluation workflows comparing LLM outputs on relevance, factual consistency, hallucination patterns, latency, and inference cost.
Extended the work toward multimodal and tool-enabled LLM systems, examining function calling and early agentic workflows, summarized into technical reports.

experience.summary: Modernized retail banking backend systems, from onboarding workflows to legacy microservices migration.
highlights: Developed backend modules in Python and PostgreSQL for retail banking applications, enabling onboarding and account servicing at scale.
Standardized reusable REST APIs across internal banking applications, cutting duplicate development effort by 35%.
Optimized SQL queries, stored procedures, and indexing, cutting report generation time by 48%.
Modernized legacy backend services into a microservices architecture, improving release flexibility by 28%.
